top_categories.workout_context: Wadi Dayqah Challenge's mixed terrain rewards steady threshold power. Surging and recovering costs more watts than just holding.
At mile 60 of 149, glycogen is gone. This workout teaches your body to produce watts on fumes.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Wadi Dayqah Challenge's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before January.
At Wadi Dayqah Challenge, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.

Road-specific control matters at Wadi Dayqah Challenge. Practice on mixed terrain: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 149 miles.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Wadi Dayqah Challenge. Train it until it feels boring.
7,014ft of climbing makes aerobic ceiling relevant when the grade or pace changes. VO2max work supports those hard moments; sustained climbing and conservative pacing remain the spine.
7,014ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
Every hard session works better with a bigger aerobic base. At 149 miles, base fitness is the difference between racing and surviving.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 7,014ft of climbing on mixed terrain does to your power file on race day.
Two threshold sessions per week without the recovery cost of VO2max work. For 149 miles, sustainable FTP gains matter more than peak power.
149 miles rewards fat oxidation. This volume work shifts your fuel mix so you're still burning fat at hour 5, not bonking at hour 3.

race_overlay.weather: January in Qurum Park, Muscat to Wadi Dayqah Dam and back, Oman. Rehearse adaptable layers and race-day kit changes in the final 2 weeks before Wadi Dayqah Challenge. Use the organizer's current forecast and safety instructions for final choices.
race_overlay.nutrition: Target 60–80g carbs/hour for Wadi Dayqah Challenge’s 149 miles. Start fueling within the first 30 minutes — early fueling prevents late-race collapse. Bonking at mile 60 is a nutrition failure, not a fitness failure.
race_overlay.altitude: Altitude may change sustainable power and recovery at Wadi Dayqah Challenge. Use conservative pacing and test any travel strategy before the event.
race_overlay.terrain: The course profile at Wadi Dayqah Challenge rewards specific practice. Include regular rides on mixed terrain to build confidence.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on TT Threshold, Durability, and Race Simulation to prepare you for 149 miles of mixed terrain in Qurum Park, Muscat to Wadi Dayqah Dam and back, Oman.
